nodes.summary: There are no positive integers $m$ and $c$ such that every element of the free group $F_2$ on generators $x, y$ is a product of at most $c$ elements, each represented by an almost $m$-palindrome, that is, by a word in $x^{\pm 1}, y^{\pm 1}$ (not necessarily reduced) that differs from a palindrome of the same length in at most $m$ positions. So the question of Kourovka Problem 19.8 has a negative answer.
nodes.title: The almost-palindromic width of $F_2$ is infinite (Kourovka 19.8)

nodes.summary: The proposition that there are positive integers $m$ and $c$ such that every element of the free group $F_2$ on generators $x, y$ is a product of at most $c$ elements, each represented by an almost $m$-palindrome, that is, by a word in $x^{\pm 1}, y^{\pm 1}$ (not necessarily reduced) that differs from a palindrome of the same length in at most $m$ positions.
nodes.title: Finite almost-palindromic width of $F_2$ (Kourovka 19.8)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, a word $w$ in the letters $x^{\pm 1}$ and $y^{\pm 1}$ is an almost $m$-palindrome if there is a palindrome $p$ in the same letters with the same length as $w$ such that $w$ and $p$ differ in at most $m$ positions. The word $w$ need not be reduced.
nodes.title: Almost palindromes
